internal.title: SEV1 Incident: High Error Rate in Checkout Service Due to Payment Service Fault Injection
internal.body:
At 11:03 UTC on 2026-11-08, an alert was triggered for a high error rate in the checkout service. Initial diagnosis identified a 50% error rate in the payment service caused by an error injection flag (paymentFailure) that led to cascading failures in checkout.

Actions taken:
- At 11:23 UTC, the paymentFailure flag was disabled after approval.
- Error rates dropped from 50% to 0.2% within minutes, confirming recovery.

The incident was resolved promptly with no further impact observed.

Next steps include a detailed postmortem and lessons learned to prevent recurrence.

external.title: Some checkouts failed due to payment processing issues
external.body: Between 11:03 and 11:23 UTC on 2026-11-08, some customers experienced failures completing checkout due to issues in the payment processing system. The issue was identified and resolved quickly by disabling a faulty configuration, restoring normal service. We apologize for any inconvenience caused.

output.impact: Some customers experienced checkout failures between 11:03 and 11:23 UTC due to payment service errors.
output.root_cause: An error injection flag (paymentFailure) in the payment service caused a high error rate (50%), which cascaded to the checkout service. Disabling this flag resolved the issue.
output.resolution: The paymentFailure flag was disabled at 11:23 UTC after approval, leading to rapid recovery of service error rates to normal levels.

lessons.lesson: Avoid deploying error injection flags in production without strict controls and rapid rollback mechanisms.
lessons.applies_when: When error injection flags are enabled in the payment service causing elevated error rates.

action_items: Implement stricter controls and monitoring for error injection flags in payment service.
Establish faster approval workflows for disabling faulty flags during incidents.
